body.proof_tex:
We give the local lower and upper arguments separately and keep the order of limits explicit.

First derive the local limit experiment.  Put \(u_+=1+c\rho_0\), \(u_-=1-c\rho_0\), both strictly positive, and
\[
 I_0=\frac{c^2}{1-c^2\rho_0^2}.
\]
Under \(\mathcal E_{\lambda_K,\rho_0}\), the two mark counts are independent Poisson variables with means \(\lambda_Ku_+/2\) and \(\lambda_Ku_-/2\).  For \(\rho=\rho_0+h/\sqrt{\lambda_K}\), Taylor expansion of the exact likelihood gives, uniformly for \(h\) in a fixed compact set,
\[
 \log\frac{f_{\lambda_K,\rho}}{f_{\lambda_K,\rho_0}}
 =h\Delta_K-\frac12h^2I_0+o_{P_{\rho_0}}(1), \tag{20}
\]
where
\[
 \Delta_K=\frac c{\sqrt{\lambda_K}}
 \left(\frac{N_+}{u_+}-\frac{N_-}{u_-}\right),
 \qquad
 \mathbb E_{\rho_0}\Delta_K=0,qquad
 \operatorname{Var}_{\rho_0}(\Delta_K)=I_0.
\]
The centered Poisson characteristic functions show \(\Delta_K\rightsquigarrow\mathcal N(0,I_0)\).  The third-order Taylor remainder in (20) is \(O_{P}(\lambda_K^{-1/2})\) on compact \(h\)-sets because \(u_\pm>0\).  If \(\Lambda_{K,h}\) is the likelihood ratio in (20), direct evaluation of the two Poisson exponential moments gives
\[
 \mathbb E_{\rho_0}\Lambda_{K,h}^2
 =\exp\left\{\frac{c^2h^2}{2}
 \left(\frac1{u_+}+\frac1{u_-}\right)\right\}
 =e^{h^2I_0}.
\]
Thus the likelihood ratios are uniformly integrable on every compact \(h\)-set.  Hence, for every finite collection of local \(h\)'s, the likelihood-ratio vector converges in \(L^1\) to that of the Gaussian shift experiment
\[
 X=-bh+\sqrt{V(\rho_0)}Z,\qquad Z\sim\mathcal N(0,1), \tag{21}
\]
for estimating the local target \(-bh\), because
\[
 \frac{b^2}{I_0}=\frac{1-c^2\rho_0^2}{16a^2}=V(\rho_0). \tag{22}
\]
For clarity, finite-prior risk convergence used below follows directly from this \(L^1\) statement.  Dominating all laws by the central law, the Bayes risk under a finite prior is the expectation of the pointwise infimum, over the action, of a finite weighted sum of bounded losses times likelihood ratios.  This infimum is Lipschitz in the likelihood-ratio vector with constant at most \(T\).  Thus its expectations converge by \(L^1\), with no appeal to unbounded-loss convergence.  The scaled image \(\sqrt{\lambda_K}(\mathcal D-(a-b\rho_0))\) exhausts \(\mathbb R\), because \(\rho_0\in(-r,r)\) and \(\mathcal A\subset\mathcal D\); restricting finite-sample actions to this image can only increase the lower Bayes bound and does not alter the limit.

We next compute the minimax value of (21) for \(\ell_T\).  Let \(Z_V\sim\mathcal N(0,V(\rho_0))\), and denote its density by \(\varphi_V\).  Put
\[
 m_T=\mathbb E\min\{Z_V^2,T\}.
\]
The translation-equivariant estimator \(X\) has constant risk \(m_T\).  Conversely, average the risk of any estimator against a uniform prior for the location on \([-A,A]\).  For \(|x|\le A-B\), the inner convolution contains all errors in \([-B,B]\); hence the average risk is at least
\[
 \left(1-\frac BA\right)
 \inf_v\int_{-B}^{B}\ell_T(v+z)\varphi_V(z)\,dz. \tag{23}
\]
Let first \(A\to\infty\), then \(B\to\infty\).  The layer-cake identity
\[
 \ell_T(x)=\int_0^T\mathbf 1\{|x|>\sqrt t\}\,dt
\]
and symmetry and unimodality of the Gaussian density show that every centered interval has maximal Gaussian probability; therefore the last infimum tends to its value at \(v=0\), namely \(m_T\).  Continuous uniform priors in (23) can be approximated by finite grids because Gaussian shift laws are continuous in total variation and the bounded loss is continuous.  Consequently, for every \(\epsilon>0\), there is a finite prior supported in some \([-G,G]\) whose Gaussian Bayes risk is at least \(m_T-\epsilon\).

We now transfer this finite prior to legal deterministic arrays.  Positivity of both arm sizes gives
\[
 \varepsilon_K\ge (n_d/K)^2\quad(d=0,1),
 \qquad
 \lambda_K/K=(n_0/K)(n_1/K)\to0.
\]
Eventually
\[
 s_K=(K\lambda_K)^{-1/4},\qquad
 \sqrt{\lambda_K}s_K=(\lambda_K/K)^{1/4}\to0,qquad
 Ks_K^2=\sqrt{K/\lambda_K}\to\infty. \tag{24}
\]
Thus \(\eta_K\to0\), and also
\[
 \sqrt{\lambda_K}\sup_{|h|\le G}
 \left|q_K(\rho_0+h/\sqrt{\lambda_K})-\rho_0-h/\sqrt{\lambda_K}\right|\to0. \tag{25}
\]
For each support point \(h\) of the finite prior, use
\(\Pi_{K,q_K(\rho_0+h/\sqrt{\lambda_K})}^{\mathrm{shell}}\).  By (24)--(25), for every fixed \(H>G+1\), all arrays in these mixture supports belong to \(\mathcal H_K(\rho_0,H)\) for all sufficiently large \(K\).  Their scaled realized-target discrepancy satisfies
\[
 \sup\sqrt{\lambda_K}|L_K-(a-bq_K)|
 \le b\sqrt{\lambda_K}s_K\to0. \tag{26}
\]
Because \(\ell_T\) is \(2\sqrt T\)-Lipschitz, (26) changes risk by \(o(1)\) at fixed \(T\).  The reverse kernel is common to all \(q\)'s, and its total-variation error is \(e_K\to0\) by (24).  Hence every full-data rule induces one marked-Poisson rule whose finite-prior Bayes risk is no larger than the full-data mixture risk plus \(Te_K+o(1)\).  The mixture risk is bounded above by the supremum over the deterministic shell.  Equations (20)--(26) and finite-prior convergence therefore give
\[
 \liminf_{K\to\infty}\inf_{D_K}
 \sup_{\mathcal H_K(\rho_0,H)}
 \mathbb E\ell_T(\sqrt{\lambda_K}(D_K-L_K))
 \ge m_T-\epsilon
\]
for every fixed \(T\) and all sufficiently large fixed \(H>G+1\).  Letting \(H\to\infty\) and then \(\epsilon\downarrow0\) proves the lower bound \(m_T\).

For the upper bound, the uniform sparse Gaussian theorem and bounded continuity of \(\ell_T\) imply, for every fixed \(H,T\),
\[
 \limsup_{K\to\infty}\sup_{\mathcal H_K(\rho_0,H)}
 \mathbb E\ell_T\!\left(
 \sqrt{\lambda_K}(\widehat L_K-L_K)
 \right)\le m_T. \tag{27}
\]
The distance from \(a-b\rho_0\) to the boundary of \(\mathcal D=[a-b,a+b]\) is positive.  On a fixed shell, consistency makes clipping asymptotically inactive, so (27) also holds for \(\operatorname{clip}_{\mathcal D}(\widehat L_K)\).  Combining the lower and upper bounds, then taking \(H\to\infty\), and only afterward using monotone convergence as \(T\to\infty\), gives
\[
 \lim_{T\to\infty}m_T=\mathbb EZ_V^2=V(\rho_0),
\]
which is the asserted ordered identity.  At no stage was an unbounded scaled loss transferred in total variation.
